title: Industrial Protocol Stack Landscape
notes: Stars and forks are snapshots taken on the verified date and cover the whole repository.
repoCreated is the GitHub repository creation date; historySince is the year of the first commit in its history, which can be older.
release is the newest stable version from the channel the project actually publishes to; source names that channel.
maintenance: active = a commit in the last 12 months, slowing = 12 to 36 months, quiet = more than 36 months; archived, deprecated and discontinued follow the project's own statement.
Capabilities list what the project documents. They are not conformance results.

protocols.name: Modbus
protocols.focus: TCP, RTU and ASCII; client and server
protocols.summary: The broadest open-source ecosystem in OT, spanning C, Python, Java, .NET, JavaScript, Rust, Go and microcontrollers.

protocols.name: OPC UA
protocols.summary: Several large independent stacks next to the OPC Foundation reference stack and a strong commercial SDK market.

protocols.name: BACnet
protocols.summary: Support differs widely by data link and by service, so one "BACnet supported" badge says very little.

protocols.name: IEC 60870-5-104
protocols.summary: A handful of credible engines, with bindings and forks built on top of them.

protocols.name: IEC 61850 / MMS
protocols.summary: Few comprehensive implementations. MMS alone is not IEC 61850.

protocols.name: Siemens S7
protocols.summary: Classic S7comm is well covered; S7commPlus for the S7-1200/1500 is only now getting open implementations.

protocols.name: OpenADR
protocols.summary: 2.0b and 3.x are different technologies, and 3.1 is not backward-compatible with 3.0.

protocols.name: OCPP
protocols.focus: Charging station to CSMS over WebSocket/JSON
protocols.summary: 2.0.1 is not backward-compatible with 1.6, while 2.1 extends 2.0.1, so a single "OCPP supported" claim says little without the version.

protocols.name: DNP3
protocols.focus: SCADA master to outstation over TCP, UDP, TLS and serial lines
protocols.maturity: Mature, with few active open stacks
protocols.summary: The long-standing open-source reference, opendnp3, is archived and its best-known successor is source-available, so the actively maintained, permissively licensed field is small and young.

implementations.name: NModbus
implementations.notes: No GitHub Release objects, but versions are tagged and published to NuGet. History goes back to the original NModbus by Scott Alexander (2006).

implementations.name: goburrow/modbus
implementations.notes: Client only. No commits since 2018; still widely imported as a reference Go client.

implementations.name: Modbus4J
implementations.notes: Commercial licences are offered by Radix IoT. The newest tag is v3.1.0 (2022) and the main branch is at 3.1.1-SNAPSHOT, ahead of the old 2.x GitHub Release. Artifacts are published to the Mango Automation Maven repository, not Maven Central.

implementations.name: ModbusMaster
implementations.notes: Arduino library for an RTU master over serial. Unchanged since 2016, still in the Arduino Library Manager.

implementations.name: modbus-esp8266
implementations.notes: ESP8266, ESP32 and other Arduino targets.

implementations.name: jsmodbus (node-modbus)
implementations.notes: Published on npm as jsmodbus. The newest git tag is v4.0.9 (2022) and the old GitHub Release is v2.0.1, so npm is the place to check. No LICENSE file in the repository; the licence comes from package.json.

implementations.name: simonvetter/modbus
implementations.notes: Versions are git tags consumed through the Go module proxy, without GitHub Release objects.

implementations.name: j2mod
implementations.notes: Fork and continuation of jamod.

implementations.name: tokio-modbus
implementations.notes: Releases are tagged and published to crates.io, without GitHub Release objects.

implementations.name: digitalpetri/modbus
implementations.notes: Added in this pass: Java 17+, by the author of Eclipse Milo. Supports Modbus/TCP Security. Stars and forks read from the repository page on 2026-10-18.

implementations.name: Triangle MicroWorks Modbus libraries
implementations.notes: Source code libraries sold as part of the Triangle MicroWorks protocol portfolio.

implementations.name: open62541
implementations.notes: Maintenance branches 1.4.x and 1.3.x get parallel patch releases.

implementations.name: OPC Foundation UA-.NETStandard
implementations.notes: The OPC Foundation reference stack. Licensed under the OPC Foundation MIT License 1.00; contributions need the Foundation CLA.

implementations.name: node-opcua
implementations.notes: Maintained by Sterfive, which also sells support and extensions.

implementations.name: opcua-asyncio (asyncua)
implementations.notes: The maintained Python successor of python-opcua; git history starts in the python-opcua code base (2015).

implementations.name: python-opcua
implementations.notes: The README marks the library deprecated and points users to opcua-asyncio.

implementations.name: async-opcua
implementations.notes: Git history starts with locka99/opcua in January 2017; the repository itself was created in December 2024.

implementations.name: locka99/opcua
implementations.notes: No commits since October 2024. The FreeOpcUa async-opcua project carries the same history forward.

implementations.name: gopcua/opcua
implementations.notes: Client first; the server package is newer and narrower than the client.

implementations.name: go-opcua
implementations.relation: Credits the gopcua authors in its MIT licence

implementations.name: Unified Automation SDKs
implementations.notes: Client and server SDKs for C, C++ and .NET.

implementations.name: Prosys OPC UA SDK for Java
implementations.notes: Commercial Java SDK built on the OPC Foundation Java stack.

implementations.name: BACnet Stack
implementations.notes: Started on SourceForge in 2004 by Steve Karg; the GitHub repository dates from 2019. Releases are published on SourceForge and tagged in git, not as GitHub Releases. The linking exception lets proprietary code link the library without becoming GPL; example applications are MIT.

implementations.name: BACpypes3
implementations.notes: Ships an optional MCP server that exposes BACnet services to AI agents. No LICENSE file; the licence is declared in pyproject.toml.

implementations.name: BACpypes
implementations.notes: PyPI has 0.19.0, newer than the last GitHub Release (v0.18.6). New work happens in BACpypes3.

implementations.name: System.IO.BACnet
implementations.notes: The stack behind the YABE explorer, originally by Morten Kvistgaard. Licence verified: MIT.

implementations.name: BACnet4J
implementations.notes: Commercial licences from Radix IoT. History reaches back to 2008 (Serotonin Software). Builds are published to the Mango Automation Maven repository.

implementations.name: ulbios/bacnet
implementations.notes: No tags or releases; consumed as a Go pseudo-version. BACnet/IP only. Builds on kazukiigeta/bacnet.

implementations.name: @bacnet-js/client
implementations.notes: Carries the Node.js BACnet lineage forward (git history from 2017, PLUS for Node-RED); maintained by Innovation-System.

implementations.name: @bacnet-js/device
implementations.relation: Device object model on top of @bacnet-js/client

implementations.name: worldiety/bacnet
implementations.notes: Added in this pass. The README calls it a prototype; no tags yet. OT Fabric runs it in bacnet-interop as a native transport and APDU layer.

implementations.name: Cimetrics BACstac
implementations.notes: Source-code and binary SDKs for Windows, Linux, .NET and embedded targets.

implementations.name: PolarSoft FreeRange
implementations.notes: Listed among the developer aids on bacnet.org.

implementations.name: SoftDEL BACnet stack
implementations.notes: Embedded BACnet stack; the linked announcement covers protocol revision 18 support.

implementations.name: lib60870
implementations.notes: Commercial licences and support from MZ Automation. Also implements IEC 60870-5-101.

implementations.name: OpenMUC j60870
implementations.notes: Distributed through OpenMUC and Maven Central rather than a public GitHub repository, so stars, forks and creation date do not apply. Proprietary licences are offered too.

implementations.name: go-iecp5 (thinkgos)
implementations.notes: Archived by its owner on 2023-03-04. Maintained forks carry it on.

implementations.name: go-iecp5 (wendy512)
implementations.notes: Added in this pass. GitHub fork of thinkgos/go-iecp5 that keeps tagging releases; its README still carries the upstream archive note.

implementations.name: wendy512/iec104
implementations.notes: Apache-2.0 itself, but it depends on LGPL-3.0 go-iecp5.

implementations.name: iec104-python (c104)
implementations.notes: Published on PyPI as c104. Fraunhofer FIT.

implementations.name: libiec61850
implementations.notes: Commercial licences and support from MZ Automation. Git history starts in 2014.

implementations.name: IEC61850bean
implementations.notes: Formerly OpenIEC61850. MMS client and server; no commits since June 2023.

implementations.name: dscsystems/go-iec61850
implementations.notes: Three months old; capabilities as claimed by its README.

implementations.name: Apache PLC4X
implementations.notes: Multi-protocol framework: stars and forks cover all of PLC4X, not only the S7 driver.

implementations.name: S7NetPlus
implementations.notes: No commits since September 2023.

implementations.name: python-snap7
implementations.relation: Wrapped Snap7 until 2.x; native Python since 3.0
implementations.notes: Rewritten in 3.0 (March 2026) as a pure Python TPKT, COTP and S7 implementation. Earlier versions wrapped the native Snap7 library.

implementations.name: gos7
implementations.notes: No tags; consumed as a Go pseudo-version. Still receiving merges in 2026.

implementations.name: Snap7
implementations.notes: By Davide Nardella, distributed on SourceForge. The GitHub repository SCADACS/snap7 (284 stars, 99 forks) is a fork with server extensions, not the canonical source.

implementations.name: s7commplus
implementations.notes: Targets S7-1200 and S7-1500; the README lists the firmware versions validated so far.

implementations.name: Softing siAccess
implementations.notes: Successor to DELTA LOGIC ACCON-AGLink after Softing acquired DELTA LOGIC; covers Siemens PLCs and SINUMERIK.

implementations.name: PLCcom for S7
implementations.notes: Editions with symbolic access for newer controllers.

implementations.name: OpenLEADR (Python)
implementations.notes: An LF Energy project.

implementations.name: OpenLEADR (Rust)
implementations.notes: VEN client library and VTN server. The README states that subscriptions (webhooks) are not supported yet.

implementations.name: ElaadNL openadr3-client
implementations.notes: From ElaadNL, the Dutch EV charging knowledge centre.

implementations.name: avob/OpenADR
implementations.notes: No tags or releases. No commits since 2021.

implementations.name: EPRI OpenADR Virtual Top Node
implementations.notes: Licence verified: BSD-3-Clause (COPYING.txt). EPRI has discontinued support; the code stays up as an example.

implementations.name: EPRI OpenADR Virtual End Node
implementations.relation: Built on the EPRI VEN library

implementations.name: EPRI OpenADR VEN Library
implementations.notes: Licence verified: BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE.txt, liboadr).

implementations.name: ocpp (The Mobility House)
implementations.notes: Asyncio library for both sides of an OCPP-J connection. The README names 1.6 and 2.0.1; release 2.1.0 added an ocpp.v21 package (PR #728).

implementations.name: Java-OCA-OCPP (ChargeTime)
implementations.notes: Client and server library. The README lists OCPP 1.6 over JSON and SOAP, 2.0.1 and 2.1. Version 2.0 moved to new Maven artifacts (java-oca-ocpp, ocpp2, ocpp-common); the older v1_6 artifacts stop at 1.1.0 from 2022. OCPP 2.1 is on master, not in the v2.0 release.

implementations.name: ocpp-go
implementations.notes: OCPP-J only, with no plans for SOAP. The README marks 2.0.1 as working in examples but needing more real-world testing.

implementations.name: libocpp (EVerest)
implementations.relation: Merged into the EVerest repository at lib/everest/ocpp
implementations.notes: Charging-station-side OCPP library. The standalone repository was archived on 2026-04-27 and development continues inside EVerest; its README says the 2.0.1 implementation has been OCA certified on several hardware platforms and 2.1 is under development. ocpp-interop runs the libocpp of everest-core 2026.02.1.

implementations.name: CitrineOS
implementations.notes: Modular CSMS server with an operator UI, RabbitMQ messaging and published container images. The README carries the OCA OCPP 2.0.1 Core and Advanced Security certification logo, and its API routes include 2.1.

implementations.name: EVerest
implementations.notes: LF Energy charging station software stack, formerly the everest-core repository. Its README lists OCPP 1.6, 2.0.1 and 2.1 next to ISO 15118-2/-20, DIN SPEC 70121 and IEC 61851.

implementations.name: SteVe
implementations.notes: Long-running open-source CSMS with a web UI. It covers OCPP 1.x only. The README notes an OCA 1.6 certification of the Powerfill backend built on SteVe, which does not apply to SteVe itself.

implementations.name: MicroOcpp
implementations.notes: OCPP client for microcontrollers such as ESP32. All 1.6 feature profiles are supported; 2.0.1 use cases are alpha and off by default. Commercial support is offered via micro-ocpp.com.

implementations.name: rust-ocpp
implementations.notes: Message types validated against the OCA JSON schemas, with no transport. The repository moved from codelabsab/rust-ocpp; 2.1 sits behind a work-in-progress feature flag.

implementations.name: ocpp-rpc
implementations.notes: Node.js client and server for the OCPP-J RPC framing, with schema validation and support for security profiles 1 to 3. Message handling beyond the RPC layer is left to the application.

implementations.name: OCPP.Core
implementations.notes: Small .NET OCPP server with a management web UI and SQL Server or SQLite storage. The README lists 1.6J, 2.0 and 2.1; the bundled 2.0 schemas are 2.0.1.

implementations.name: Open OCPP
implementations.notes: C++ library for charge points, central systems and local controllers. The 1.x line keeps the 1.6 API; 2.0.0-alpha on the develop branch adds 2.0.1 with a new API.

implementations.name: OpenOCPP (ChargeLab)
implementations.notes: Embedded charger firmware released by CSMS vendor ChargeLab in June 2025, with an ESP32 demo. The README reports passing the OCTT 2.0.1 core test cases as part of a vendor declaration of conformance.

implementations.name: ocpp-toolkit (IZIVIA)
implementations.notes: Kotlin library from French operator IZIVIA with a generic API across OCPP versions. The charging station side of 1.6 and 2.0.1 is complete over OCPP-J; security features beyond HTTP basic auth are not.

implementations.name: WWCP_OCPP (Open Charging Cloud)
implementations.notes: Library with CSMS, charging station, local controller and gateway roles, plus its own OCPP CSE vendor extensions. 2.0.1 is served through the 2.1 code; no releases or tags are published.

implementations.name: library-ocpp (Monta)
implementations.notes: OCPP library published by charging platform Monta and distributed through JitPack. The README documents the server-initiated message API.

implementations.name: e-mobility charging stations simulator (SAP)
implementations.notes: Node.js simulator that runs many OCPP-J charging stations for CSMS load and conformance testing. The repository also ships a small mock OCPP server.

implementations.name: Home Assistant OCPP integration
implementations.relation: Built on the mobilityhouse ocpp library
implementations.notes: Home Assistant integration that acts as a central system for local chargers. Its manifest requires ocpp>=2.1.0.

implementations.name: Open e-Mobility (ev-server)
implementations.notes: Node.js CSMS backend from SAP Labs France with smart charging, billing and roaming. The repository is archived; OCPP 2.0 was planned but never added.

implementations.name: NewMotion OCPP (Scala)
implementations.notes: OCPP-J library developed and used by NewMotion, later Shell Recharge. It is archived; the README notes only partial 2.0 support and a separate library for SOAP.

implementations.name: Motown
implementations.notes: Early open-source charging back office with OCPP and OCPI modules. No commits since 2019.

implementations.name: Trialog QOCPP
implementations.notes: OCPP communication stacks sold in two variants: QOCPP-CS for charging stations and QOCPP-CSMS for supervisors. Both are C++ on Qt; the datasheets list 2.1 bidirectional charging as a prototype licence option.

implementations.name: Delta OCPP Stack
implementations.notes: Portable OCPP stack offered by Delta Electronics (Thailand) as automotive middleware, with 2.1 on its roadmap. Language and licensing terms are not published.

implementations.name: ByteSnap OCPP software
implementations.notes: UK design house offering an OCPP client and library for chargers, as a product or under a customised software licence. The page names OCPP 1.6 and 2.0 without further detail.

implementations.name: go-ocpp
implementations.notes: Both roles on one RPC engine, every action typed and validated against the OCA schemas, including the 2.1 SEND and CALLRESULTERROR. Tested against the five ocpp-interop references.

implementations.name: dnp3 (Step Function I/O)
implementations.notes: Rust core with C, C++, .NET and Java bindings, also published to NuGet and Maven Central. The licence allows non-commercial, non-production use; production use needs a commercial licence from Step Function I/O. No Secure Authentication.

implementations.name: opendnp3
implementations.notes: For a decade the de facto open-source DNP3 stack, with Java and .NET bindings. Archived on 1 September 2022 at 3.1.2; still the engine under several Python bindings and forks. Secure Authentication was removed in 2016.

implementations.name: go-dnp3 (DSC Systems)
implementations.notes: Pure Go master and outstation with Secure Authentication v5 (no aggressive mode), file transfer, data sets and multi-drop, plus command-line tools. Runs the DNP Users Group IED conformance procedures in CI. Pre-1.0: the README says the API is not yet stable.

implementations.name: dnp3py
implementations.notes: Pure Python on asyncio, targeting the level 2 subset, with a MESA IEEE 1815.2 DER outstation simulator. In dnp3-interop its outstation serves only a reduced fixture.

implementations.name: dnp3 (cB-Sigma)
implementations.notes: Pure Go master and outstation written for the SigmaM2M oneM2M platform, with Secure Authentication v5 including update key changes and user certificates, a gateway and device profile documents. Interop tested against opendnp3 by its authors. A companion module, dnp3-sim, is a fault-injecting simulated outstation built on it.

implementations.name: nfm-dnp3
implementations.notes: Small pure Python master over TCP: class polls, binary, analog and counter points, direct operate and select-before-operate. Imported as dnp3py, a different project from craigpnnl's dnp3py. MIT per its PyPI metadata; the repository has no licence file.

implementations.name: yadnp3
implementations.relation: Fork of opendnp3 with Python bindings
implementations.notes: "Yet another opendnp3 fork": continues the archived stack with new features (file transfer, device attributes, deadbands on the master) and pybind11 Python bindings as its focus. Describes itself as experimental.

implementations.name: pydnp3
implementations.notes: The original pybind11 bindings for opendnp3. VOLTTRON's dnp3-python continued them.

implementations.name: dnp3-python (VOLTTRON)
implementations.relation: Continuation of pydnp3, used by the VOLTTRON platform
implementations.notes: Python wrapper of opendnp3 from the VOLTTRON project (PNNL). Every PyPI release is a beta.

implementations.name: dnp3 (Dart and Flutter)
implementations.relation: Dart FFI bindings for Step Function I/O dnp3
implementations.notes: Own code MIT; it links the Step Function I/O library, so its non-commercial licence applies to apps built with it.

implementations.name: dnp3 (Green Energy Corp)
implementations.notes: The Green Energy Corp code base that opendnp3 grew out of; its history continues in the opendnp3 repository.

implementations.name: Triangle MicroWorks DNP3 libraries
implementations.notes: ANSI C source code library for masters and outstations, with .NET components as an alternative. Widely used in IEDs and SCADA products. 3.34 (July 2026) adds TLS settings for full IEC 62351-3 conformance. Its dnp3-interop adapter is on hold: the licensed source has no agreed way into the builds yet.

implementations.name: FreyrSCADA DNP3
implementations.notes: ANSI C stack for Windows, Linux and QNX with C++, C# and Python APIs, sold as source or as compiled libraries; free evaluation SDKs and simulators are distributed on GitHub and SourceForge.

implementations.name: JPEmbedded DNP3 Library
implementations.notes: C++ source code with C, C++ and Java APIs and a hardware abstraction layer, so it runs with or without an operating system; listed in ST's partner programme for STM32 microcontrollers. Claims level 4 and IEC 62351 security.

implementations.name: Beanit DNP3
implementations.notes: Pure Java library from the makers of IEC61850bean and j60870, sold under a commercial licence with a time-limited demo.

implementations.name: CODESYS DNP3 SL
implementations.notes: Makes a CODESYS controller a DNP3 outstation, licensed per device; needs a CODESYS runtime for Linux 4.10 or later. Master support is announced, not released.

implementations.name: go-dnp3
implementations.notes: Both roles with no dependencies outside the standard library: file transfer, device attributes, multi-drop, dual end point and Secure Authentication v5 with aggressive mode and statistics. Tested against the four dnp3-interop references.
